stories.title: Find the break-even line before an AI feature gets designed
stories.blurb: Victor Yocco opens with a health insurer whose AI-written appeal determinations took specialists longer to check than to write; a second version that only surfaced relevant policy and precedent cut review time. Same model, different slice of the task. Yocco’s four questions locate a break-even line: the attention a feature costs has to come back, for instance as errors caught or consistency across people.

sources.name: Smashing Magazine
sources.headline: Should You Actually Add AI To That? A Four-Question Audit For Product Teams

stories.title: Converting Carbon’s button to Figma takes 30 seconds, passing the check takes a month
stories.blurb: TJ Pitre reports that 40 of 84 generated variants passed a visual check against the original. Tuned on known kits the engine scored about 70%, on an unseen kit about 13%, so the team now works one design system at a time and lets the converter refuse rather than guess.

sources.name: TJ Pitre
sources.headline: Why a Button Takes a Month
sources.author: TJ Pitre

stories.title: Rival 50: the challenger playbook no longer sets brands apart
stories.blurb: Rival screened 2,039 brands with Imperial College and names four moves behind this year’s leaders: flipping the category’s emotional code, building from inside a microculture, shipping the brand deliberately unfinished, and designing for disagreement. A press release, but the criteria are usable as a positioning checklist.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: The Challenger Playbook Is Now Table Stakes. Rival s 2026 Index Reveals What Comes Next

stories.title: Springetts at 50: design brands for longevity, not novelty
stories.blurb: The agency behind Frubes and The Happy Egg Co. publishes a field guide built on restraint: tie new ideas to what customers already recognise instead of tearing the brand up every few years. Its framework sorts brands into life stages, each with its own job, starting with launch, grow and extend.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: What 50 years in business has taught Springetts about building brands that thrive

stories.title: Tomy becomes Takara Tomy worldwide, with a symbol few can read
stories.blurb: The first rebrand in 20 years unifies the name and replaces the blue wordmark with a gradient symbol built from the katakana for “asobi”, play. The quieter idea sits in the wordmark, where every T and A is drawn slightly differently; the symbol itself is puzzling people even in Japan.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: The toy company Tomy has a new logo, and people are baffled

stories.title: GDC survey: 22% of game developers use generative AI for concept art
stories.blurb: Overall use rose to 40% from 36%, mostly for research, summaries and code; only 8% use it for final assets. A third of respondents say they were laid off in the past two years.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: More game developers are starting to use generative AI

stories.title: Chatbots send shoppers to fake and lapsed brand domains
stories.blurb: In 6,795 answers about 151 brands, Perplexity showed risky sites in 15% of answers, ChatGPT in 8% and Gemini in 4%, including old brand domains re-registered by others. Smaller brands were hit about twice as often. The study comes from an IP protection firm with its own prompts.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds

stories.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces Flash and outscores Argon
stories.blurb: Google prices the fast model at $1.50 per million input tokens and puts it slightly above the larger Argon on the Artificial Analysis index. A new Orchestrator in Antigravity switches between Carbon and Hydrogen within one session.
